manual.title: Maximus: The Hundred Worlds - Courier Manual

pages.head: The Light Went Out
pages.html:
Maximus: The Hundred Worlds

Sector Zero, the year the stars went quiet.

For ten thousand years the Maximus Core burned at the heart of the galaxy: a forge-star whose light ran down the warp lanes to every inhabited world. Couriers rode that light from planet to planet, carrying everything from seed grain to love letters.

Then the Core cracked. Its light was held in ten star-shards, and when it broke they were flung across the Hundred Worlds. The warp lanes are failing. Sector by sector, the galaxy is going quiet.

Max is a courier at Maxima Station. Couriers deliver. This time the package is the light of the galaxy: find the ten shards, carry them through the gates, fly the Maelstrom, and bring them home to the Heart.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Installing

Copy every file on the disk into one directory, for example C:\MAXIMUS, and type MAXIMUS. You need a 386 or better with VGA and 640K. A Sound Blaster plays the music and the digitized effects; without one, the PC speaker plays them.

The menu

  • Play starts at Maxima Station's training deck.
  • Read Instructions, Read Storyline and See Credits show the pages from this manual on screen.
  • Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Max shows you around the training deck himself.

The training deck

The deck teaches as you go: walk, hop the crates, pick up credits, shoot the practice drones, pay the credit door, ride the lift and walk into the airlock. Then you are in the pod.

One thing stands between the lift and the airlock: the clearance gate. Climb the ledge to the clerk's window and step into it for your departure form, which stamps a dock, a world and a courier badge. Set the dock, the world and the badge on the Courier's Star Wheel from the box, read its two windows in order, and press the one hatch of the three that wears the same two pictures. The wrong hatches only sigh and send you back, so a courier without the wheel can simply try them in turn.

Lives and saving

You start with 3 lives and 100 hit points. Lose them all and the signal is lost. Save often with F5: it is a big galaxy.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Keys

Left RightWalk, swim, drive or thrust
UpJet hop on foot (tap again in the air to climb), thrust in the pod and the bell, jump with Spring Shocks in the rover
DownCurl into a ball (on foot), dive, brake
SpaceFire, in the direction you last moved
G / BPick up / drop a module
THail (say hello)
F1Help
F2Status: score, credits, hit points, lives and your modules
F3 / F4Music / sound on and off
F5 / F6Save / load
EscQuit

The number pad's 8 4 6 2 work the same as the arrows. W/A/S/D are not a second set of arrows here: W fires the Flak Cannon. Pick up with G and drop with B, under the left hand while the right steers and away from W/A/S/D, so a WASD habit can't throw a module away.

Module keys

ZPlasma Lance
XNova Core
Q / EDash Boots
CShield Emitter
FHover Pack
VMine Layer
RMed Kit
WFlak Cannon
Q / E (sub)Hydro Jets
Up (rover)Spring Shocks

pages.head: Four Ways to Travel
pages.html:
The courier pod

Space charts are flown in the pod. The arrows fire its thrusters; let go and it brakes. Fly into the middle of a planet to land, into a warp ring to jump.

On foot

Max's suit has grav-jets: Up is a hop, and another tap in the air hops again. Hold Right while you tap Up to sail over gaps. Walk into the uplink beacon behind you to return to orbit.

The diving bell

On sea worlds Max takes the bell. It swims at a steady pace with the arrows and holds still when you let go. Bubble columns lift you, currents push you. Surface at the buoy to leave.

The rover

Rover worlds are fast and flat. The rover rides the lifts at every step; with the Spring Shocks module it can jump.

pages.head: The Galaxy and the Shards
pages.html:
Sector gates

The galaxy chart holds five sector warps around the dead Core. The Cradle is open; every other sector is sealed by crystal gates, two to a sector. A gate opens when you touch it carrying its shard, and the shards stay with you for good.

SectorGate needsWorlds
1. The Cradleopen18
2. EmberreachRuby + Amber18
3. The ShallowsCitrine + Emerald18
4. GlasswindJade + Aqua18
5. The Deep BlackSapphire + Amethyst16
The Coreall ten3

Jump rings

Every sector chart also holds a jump ring, walled in behind the next sector's crystal gates: carry those shards and it takes you straight on. The ring in The Deep Black leads to the Maelstrom itself.

Finding shards

Planets with a gold signal beside them on the sector chart hold a shard, deep in a vault. The planet card you see on landing says where you are (SECTOR 2 OF 5, WORLD 9 OF 18), names the shard and which of the ten it is (SHARD 3 OF 10), reminds you that F5 saves, and its long-range scan shows the whole world: where you land (green) and where the vault lies (gold).

The Core

All ten shards open the way to the Core. Fly the Maelstrom, a storm canyon so packed with rock that your weapons jam, to the Citadel, whose vault holds the teleporter to the Heart. There the Guardian's armor plates stand across the hall, and down their middle runs a seal of light that opens only to the Core's own spark. The Heart Eye circles in front of it and swoops when you come near. Crack it three times, with a plasma bolt, a shield orb or by ramming it (that hurts), and it bursts into the Core Light, which finds you and charges the seal: then walk through. Plasma cracks the plates; shouldering into them works too, for a few hit points.

Trading posts

Each chart has a trading post. Nudge a pad to buy: an extra life (100 credits), repairs (20), plasma cells (30), nova charges (40), shield charges (30) and med kits (50). One of each per visit.

pages.head: Worlds and Vaults
pages.html:
What you will find

  • Credits (green chips), gems (score), hearts (hit points), 1-Ups and ammo cells for your modules.
  • Vaults deep underground hold the shards and modules. A credit door costs 10 credits to open; a force field blinks on and off.
  • Crystal walls shatter at a touch, and some rock is not rock at all: secret pockets hide treasure.
  • Lifts and bubble columns carry you up; winds and currents push you along.
  • Lava, acid and brine hurt, but the jolt hops you out. A healing spring in the caves mends 100 hit points in one long drink, then runs dry until you land on that world again.
  • Nests in cave walls send out creatures until you leave.

pages.head: Courier Modules
pages.html:
The ten modules

Modules lie in planet vaults. Press G to pick one up; it stays in your inventory (F2) and works in every vehicle that can use it.

ModuleKeyWhere
Plasma LanceZLittle Hollow, The Cradle
Nova CoreXPyre, Emberreach
Dash BootsQ / ECopperfield, The Cradle
Shield EmitterCMistral Isle, The Shallows
Hover PackFScorchmark, Emberreach
Mine LayerVRimefall, Glasswind
Med KitROutpost Nine, The Cradle
Flak CannonWVenom Marsh, Glasswind
Hydro JetsQ / E (sub)Tidewater, The Shallows
Spring ShocksUp (rover)Redrock, Emberreach

Ammunition counts carry from vehicle to vehicle. The Plasma Lance is the only weapon that cracks armor; the Shield Emitter's guard orb stops almost anything.

pages.head: Creatures
pages.html:
On the worlds

GloopA hopping slime. Harmless alone, never alone.
Gloop MotherSplits into a Gloopling when shot.
GlooplingSmall, fast, and it follows you.
ShellbackA beetle walking its beat.
IronbackArmored. Blaster bolts bounce off; use the Plasma Lance.
DropwebHangs from cave ceilings and drops on you.
FlitterA cave bat with no sense of direction.
ScreechA bigger bat that dives when you come near.
StingerWasps home in on courier suits.

In the seas

MinnowSmall fry darting about in schools.
SnapfinA toothy little fish that comes straight for you.
BigfinCruises back and forth along the reef.
AnglerWaits in the dark, then lunges at your lamp.
Ribbon EelSwims long laps through open water.
MorayLurks in holes and snaps at passers-by.

In space

Void JellyDrifts between the stars.
Void MiteTiny, fast and drawn to engines.
Pirate SkiffFlies a patrol line.
Pirate AceHunts couriers for their cargo.
RaiderFlies figure eights around its loot.
Scout DroneWanders and watches.

On the stations

CrawlerA maintenance bot gone bad.
Sentry DroneWanders the corridors.
Gun TurretBolted to the deck. Armored.
Security BotArmored patroller.
Spider BotDrops from the ceiling.
Hover MineBobs in place.

Star whales are gentle and swim in pods. Every whale in a pod follows the same loop at the same moment, so a pod keeps its shape: look for thirteen of them circling on the galaxy chart, and for a pod in The Cradle that spells somebody's name.

Most creatures burst when they hit you. A few things - flytraps, magma, tumbling asteroids, the Phantom - cannot be hurt at all: keep moving.

Credits

Designed and built by Claude for Sandbox Software, with Game-Maker 2.0 by Recreational Software Designs. Every world, sprite, song and sound was made by a program from a seed.

Hails

Three worlds call you before you land. Galileo is an old Earth probe still running a loop on its RCA 1802 (the real chip flew to Jupiter). Liberty keeps a cracked bell under thirteen stars, and an archive of every letter a courier ever brought. On Boxcar Flats, Doc Leo, PhD (Comedic Science), will walk your parcel over with his rubber chicken. Answer them all!

Dedicated to three real couriers: Lewis's mother, a letter carrier; his father, who kept the post office running in maintenance; and his grandmother, a postal clerk. All three were at the post office when he bought Game-Maker in 1992.

pages.head: Pushing the Limits
pages.html:
How far Game-Maker goes

Maximus was built to stand on every edge of Game-Maker 2.0. These are the limits we found in its file formats and in PLAYGAME, and how much of each this game uses (also in LIMITS.TXT on the disk).

LimitMaximumMaximus uses
Scenes in a .GAM231 (PLAYGAME allocates all scenes in one 64K block of 283-byte records)100: title, ending, training deck, galaxy, 5 sectors, 88 worlds, Maelstrom, Citadel, Heart, with four one-page scenes besides (Between Worlds and the three pages of the clearance gate). We stopped at 100: 28300 bytes of scene records sit easily in DOS memory, every scene still loads in a moment, and the integrator's 310x165 world view still shows each scene box and link

items.intro: Every world in the five sectors, how you get around on it, and what its vault holds. Gold signal worlds hold a shard; module vaults hold courier gear.

items.title: The Courier's Star Wheel
items.note: Three discs: a dock, a world and a courier badge give a two-picture clearance code
items.heading: THE COURIER'S STAR WHEEL · Maxima Station clearance codes
howto: Every departure form on Maxima Station carries three stamps: a dock letter, a world of origin and a courier badge.
Turn the big disc until the form's dock letter is under the arrow, the middle disc until its world is, and the small disc until its badge is.

The small disc has two windows. Read them in order, FIRST then SECOND: each shows a picture. Over a printed spot on the middle disc a window shows that picture; over a hole it looks through to the big disc. Press the hatch in the pod bay that wears the same two pictures, top to bottom.

puzzles.ask: Maxima Station's pod bay: the clerk's form says dock F, world Prism, badge Chevron. Which of the three hatches opens?
puzzles.answer: The heart, then the bolt: the middle hatch, the one between the rocket pair and the heart-and-key. The others only sigh.

items.title: Maximus Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Find your question, then slide the red film over the answer under it. Read one answer at a time: a courier who knows everything has nothing left to find.

hints.q: How do I get off the training deck?
hints.a: Pay the credit door with the credits you pick up, ride the lift, and get through the clearance gate in the pod bay (see the next question). Then walk into the airlock. The pod is waiting.

hints.q: Which of the three hatches in the pod bay opens?
hints.a: Climb the ledge to the clerk's window and step into it: the form shows your dock, world and badge. Turn the Courier's Star Wheel from the box to that world and badge and read its CODE window; the hatch wearing that picture is the one. No wheel? It is the middle one. The others only sigh and send you back, and nothing is lost.

hints.q: How do I land on a planet?
hints.a: Fly the pod into the middle of the planet on the sector chart.

hints.q: How do I get back to space?
hints.a: Walk into the uplink beacon behind you where you landed. On sea worlds, surface at the buoy.

hints.q: I keep running out of lives.
hints.a: Buy an extra life at the trading post for 100 credits, and save with F5 before every vault.

hints.q: Where is the Ruby shard?
hints.a: Ambermoor, in The Cradle. Look for the gold signal on the sector chart, then use the long-range scan on the planet card to find the vault.

hints.a: Hot Springs, in Emberreach. Look for the gold signal on the sector chart, then use the long-range scan on the planet card to find the vault.

hints.q: Where do I find the Plasma Lance?
hints.a: In a vault on Little Hollow, in The Cradle. Press G to pick it up; its key is Z.

hints.q: Where do I find the Nova Core?
hints.a: In a vault on Pyre, in Emberreach. Press G to pick it up; its key is X.

hints.q: Where do I find the Dash Boots?
hints.a: In a vault on Copperfield, in The Cradle. Press G to pick it up; its key is Q / E.

hints.q: Where do I find the Shield Emitter?
hints.a: In a vault on Mistral Isle, in The Shallows. Press G to pick it up; its key is C.

hints.q: Where do I find the Hover Pack?
hints.a: In a vault on Scorchmark, in Emberreach. Press G to pick it up; its key is F.

hints.q: My blaster bounces off a creature.
hints.a: It is armored, like an Ironback or a Gun Turret. Only the Plasma Lance (Z) cracks armor.

hints.q: The rover cannot climb a ledge.
hints.a: Find the Spring Shocks on Redrock in Emberreach. Then Up makes the rover jump.

hints.q: A wall of rock blocks the way to a vault.
hints.a: Walk into it. Some rock is not rock at all, and crystal walls shatter at a touch.

hints.q: How do I reach the Maelstrom?
hints.a: Open the crystal gates in The Deep Black with the Sapphire and Amethyst shards; its jump ring leads to the Maelstrom.

hints.q: Something in the Maelstrom cannot be hurt.
hints.a: The Phantom, magma and tumbling asteroids cannot be hurt at all. Keep moving.

hints.q: The Guardian's seal won't open.
hints.a: Only the Core's own light opens it. Crack the Heart Eye three times: a plasma bolt or a shield orb does it cleanly, and ramming it works but hurts. Each time it reels away, then comes back faster. The third time its light flies to you, and the seal opens at a touch.

hints.q: Some say the felt-maker left something behind...
hints.a: Fly to where the galaxy chart's four corners meet. The chart wraps around, so all four corners are one place, as far from the Core as space goes.

hints.q: I'm there. It's just a knot of asteroids.
hints.a: Rock is not always rock. Try the knot's south face. And keep a module slot free: if you're full, drop one with O first.

hints.q: Plot me a course.
hints.a: Fly to the corner of the galaxy chart and come at the knot from below. The two rocks in the middle of its south face are only a picture: fly straight up through them. Inside, press G to pick up the felt egg, then touch the beacon.

items.title: Courier license
items.name: MAX
items.back: This courier carries the light of the galaxy. Every station, port and outpost shall grant safe docking and a hot meal. Couriers deliver.

items.title: Dispatch orders
items.letterhead: MAXIMA STATION · OFFICE OF THE STATION MASTER
items.body:
Max,

You have heard the news by now: the Core has cracked and the warp lanes are failing. Every courier on the ring has been grounded except you, because you are the only one who has flown all five sectors and come back with the cargo intact.

Your orders are simple and impossible. Find the ten star-shards. Carry them through the crystal gates, sector by sector. Fly the Maelstrom. Bring them home to the Heart.

The pod is fueled. The trading posts will take your credits. Hail anyone you meet; most of them will be glad to see a courier.

Couriers deliver. Deliver this one.

items.title: The Galactic Courier
items.headline: THE CORE GOES DARK
items.deck: Warp lanes failing sector by sector; ten star-shards scattered across the Hundred Worlds

photo.caption: Verdance, where the sky went dark first.

columns:
MAXIMA STATION - The Maximus Core, the forge-star that has lit the galaxy for ten thousand years, cracked at 0400 station time. Its light, held in ten star-shards, was flung across the Hundred Worlds.

Within the hour the lanes to Emberreach went quiet. By nightfall The Shallows had stopped answering.

"We have never lost a lane before," said a dock chief at the station, who asked not to be named. "Now we are losing them one after another."

The Courier Corps has grounded all but one pilot. Station sources confirm the courier known as Max has been given the job of bringing the shards home.

Traders at Waystation Ceres report pirate skiffs moving into the empty lanes. Couriers are advised to fly armed.

Crystal gates have reportedly sealed every sector beyond The Cradle. Scholars believe each gate answers only to its own pair of shards.
briefs: Verdance farmers report hopping slimes in record numbers. Harmless alone; never alone.
The old station in The Shallows keeps its light burning, though nobody has heard from its crew.
Extra lives 100 credits, repairs 20, med kits 50. One of each per visit.

news.head: Maximus: 100 scenes, and not one more
news.html: Maximus: The Hundred Worlds is out. The Maximus Core has gone dark, and Max, a courier at Maxima Station, must carry ten star-shards home across 88 worlds by pod, on foot, by rover and in a diving bell. Game-Maker holds up to 231 scenes; we stopped at 100: a galaxy chart, five sector charts, 88 worlds, the Maelstrom, the Citadel and the Heart, plus a title, a training deck and an ending. Every limit we found is in LIMITS.TXT on the disk.

news.head: Courier’s corner
news.html: Registered couriers: your fold-out galaxy chart, the sector map of all 88 worlds and the hint book are in this box. Fold the chart along the creases and keep it by the keyboard.

news.head: Since last issue: GLITCH is gone
news.html: Virus Blaster pilots have been posting high scores on the BBS since July. Your favorite boss is the Feedback Howler; your least favorite is the Head Crash and its rings of platter shards. And the question everybody asks: can the BLASTER stop? No. The data stream never stops flowing. Pull Down to brake.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: A clown on the line
news.html: While we were building the hails in Maximus, a friend of the office asked to be in one. So on Boxcar Flats you'll meet Doc Leo, PhD (Comedic Science), a hobo clown with a rubber chicken on a leash. Doc Leo is a proud member of the Clown Club, twists balloon animals for the kids at every parade, and parks a little red electric car out front. He says he'll be in more games. We believe him.

news.head: In the workshop: Teddy gets a game
news.html: Remember Teddy, the SysOp's corgi? He's getting his own game, and it starts on the Fourth of July. Sandcastle Knight puts him in a tin helmet with a red plume as the knight of the backyard sandbox, with four castles to win back. Who knocked them down? Somebody with a lot of zoomies. You'll meet her next issue.

news.head: Letters: "Only in an emergency"
news.html:
"I told my mom I was shrinking down into the family 486 to fight a virus. She said to be home for dinner." - A pilot, by modem

The Scoop replies: Good advice. VACCINE.EXE is only for emergencies, and so is skipping dinner.

16.long: With the Dash Boots, dash left. With the Hydro Jets, burst left in the diving bell.
